---
title: Build-time content versions
description: How each build turns a docs folder into an immutable content version the site serves.
icon: Network
---

This framework serves one documentation site from one deployment. Content is
**ingested at build time**: the build reads the docs folder, compiles every
page once, and stores the result as an immutable **content version** in
Postgres. Request-time rendering reads those stored artifacts, so a page never
recompiles MDX while a visitor waits.

## How content flows

1. You push MDX (plus optional `meta.json` ordering files) and a `docs.json`
   configuration to your repository.
2. The build reads the docs folder, validates it (frontmatter schema,
   component allow-list, broken links), compiles every page once, and
   persists a new **content version** keyed by the commit SHA.
3. The serving pointer flips to the new version in one transaction — readers
   never see a half-published state.
4. A build that fails validation stops before the pointer moves, so broken
   docs never silently replace the last good version.

Every surface — HTML, `.md` routes, `llms.txt`, search, MCP, sitemaps —
resolves through the same loader, so they always agree on which version is
live.

## Rebuilding the same commit

Ingest is keyed by the content SHA. Rebuilding a commit that already has a
version reuses it instead of compiling again; force a fresh ingest when the
pipeline itself changed.

## Keeping old versions

Older versions stay in the database so a rollback is a pointer move, not a
rebuild. Garbage collection keeps the most recent versions and removes the
rest once nothing points at them.

## Why nothing is prerendered

Pages render on request from the stored version and cache on the CDN with a
short freshness window and a long stale-while-revalidate window — new content
appears shortly after a deploy, with no cache purging.
